notes: Full test du 23/11 (boîte vide, aucun post neuf du compte modèle à la veille du lundi : dernier post le 1/11) : « Job Tierlist For Optimal Health (Science based) », sa famille à 357 k (8/10) et 316 k (10/10), « Job » en rouge comme lui ; métiers à nous ; `source` gardée pour mémoire, non envoyée. Croquis de couverture neuf (metiers.jpg, Seedream). Slide Atala (11) : le premier S tier « Running Coach », deux coureuses de la banque et le logo d'Atala. Texte selon placement_atala : titre de 6 mots → voix TU (bm-001 : l'allure ; bm-002 : la séance déjà prévue ; bm-003 : le plan à ton niveau) ; ici un seul argument : les sorties calées sur les jours où tu es libre ; version « cta D' ». Faits : le travail de nuit désynchronise l'horloge circadienne et s'associe à un sommeil plus pauvre et à des risques pour la santé (revues sur le travail posté, Kecklund & Axelsson BMJ 2016) ; la sédentarité prolongée est associée à une moins bonne santé, les pauses actives l'atténuent (Ekelund et al., Lancet 2016) ; la lumière du jour cale l'horloge interne. Rien de médical. Photos : banque de l'OS, aucune célébrité, aucune marque lisible.

paragraphes: Working through the night goes against your internal clock. Your body is told to sleep while you're working, and to wake up while you're trying to rest.
Years of it are linked to poorer sleep and worse health. Few jobs fight your biology this hard.
Hours in the same seat, eyes on the road, with almost no movement and little daylight on the skin.
Long sitting with no breaks is one of the habits most linked to poor health. Here, it's the whole job.
Most of the day spent sitting, often with lunch at the desk and barely a few hundred steps.
It's not the desk that hurts you, it's never leaving it. Short walking breaks change a lot.
No commute sounds great, but it also means no walk to work and days where you barely leave one room.
It only stays in D because you can fix it: a walk before you start, outside, every day.
On your feet all day and always moving, so it's far from a sitting job.
Late nights, heat and endless shifts pull it down. Movement alone doesn't make a job healthy.
Standing, walking between desks, never really sitting still. Your body is far more active than in an office.
It stays in C because the stress and the marking often follow you home at night.
Physical work, outside, in daylight. Digging, carrying and kneeling keep your whole body busy.
It misses A tier because it's hard on the back and knees when it's done for years.
Hours of walking outside every day, whatever the weather, with plenty of daylight.
It's steady movement, but rarely hard enough to really push your heart and lungs.
Days spent outside, walking on uneven ground, with natural light setting your internal clock.
It only misses S tier because the work isn't always as active as it looks.
Hours outside at an easy pace, every week, with your heart and lungs doing the work.
No need for the job. A running coach app like Atala plans your runs on the days you're free.
Long climbs at a steady effort, fresh air, daylight and your own weight to carry.
The most active job on this list, and the one where staying fit is simply part of the work.
